routeSelection.basis: The normalized source registration is B Archeologie with teaching language Dutch. The adopted 2026–27 OER formally distinguishes the Dutch-language Archeologie trajectory from English-language Archaeology; the Dutch trajectory and its 12-EC Bachelorscriptie Archeologie are selected.

alternatives.label: Ancient societies & material culture
alternatives.concept: Studies ancient societies through world and Greek archaeology, ancient democratic heritage, history, literary sources and material and visual culture. Three archaeology and ancient-heritage courses provide 22.5 EC. GIS and soils add environmental landscape methods. This is substantive related study, with gaps in systematic European period coverage, excavation, archaeological science and an archaeology thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: Three archaeology/ancient-heritage courses lead a broader composition in ancient societies, material and visual culture, written evidence and landscape methods. The label does not promise a full Archaeology degree.
progression: All24placementsverifiedintheactualworkbook,includinggatewaybeforeEarthObservation;sevenadvancedcoursesandYear1PPD. Foundationarchaeology/art/literatureprecedesadvancedheritageandinterpretation. GIS/soilworkisenvironmental,notarchaeologicalfieldqualification;Walcherenhistoryresearchisnotanarchaeologythesis. Western Art History is moved to semester1 before Renaissance Italy in semester2; History of Empires moves to semester3, preserving exact fall offerings.

alternatives.label: Cultural heritage, museums & public memory
alternatives.concept: Studies how material culture is interpreted and contested through archaeology, African heritage and restitution, modern art museums, art-historical interpretation, ethics and public communication. Sociology and qualitative inquiry support community perspectives. Modern US racial history and its research podcast supply a specific wider context, not archaeological heritage training. Rhetoric in Action currently involves work mainly in Dutch at a local primary school.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum concentrates on museums, heritage ethics, public memory, restitution, community interpretation and documentary communication. The label reflects that institutional and public-facing emphasis.
alternatives.distinctness: The programmes share17courses;sevenunique courses(52.5EC)each. The closest adds ancient literary/history interpretation and environmental GIS/soil/data foundations; the heritage direction adds rhetoric,stylistics,sociology,qualitative inquiry and ethics to organise questions of institutions,ownership and public interpretation. Modern race/media is a specific contextual contribution,not archaeological methods. Numericaldifferencealoneisnotthejustification.

notes.text: Both UCR programmes offer substantive related study of objects, past societies and cultural interpretation. Neither reproduces the full Archaeology bachelor: systematic European period coverage, excavation and field schools, archaeological materials science and the required archaeology thesis remain gaps. Optional independent research is separate, requires approval and is outside the 24-course, 180-EC schedules; it does not replace the VU thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Archaeology studies past societies through material remains, historical evidence and landscapes. The programme combines Mediterranean and European archaeology with scientific and digital methods, two field schools, critical heritage study and an individual archaeology thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers two substantive related compositions: ancient societies and material culture, and cultural heritage, museums and public interpretation. Their three archaeology and ancient-heritage courses connect with art, history and source interpretation. Environmental GIS and soils are complementary methods; general communication is not heritage management. Neither programme supplies VU’s full period sequence, excavation, archaeological materials science or required thesis.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC comprises 138 EC of required courses, a 12 EC thesis including its compulsory colloquium, and 30 EC of free academic choice. Thesis entry requires completion of all first- and second-year courses. Field School 1 requires What is Archaeology; Field School 2 requires Field School 1. Listed practicals require 85% attendance or applicable replacement work. A first-year language test and remediation when needed carry no extra credits. The usual first-year study-advice threshold is 48 EC. Free-choice level, overlap and approval rules apply.

componentNotes.thesis: Required 12 EC individual Dutch-language thesis, including the compulsory colloquium. The English-language thesis is the alternative for the English route, not an additional component.
